title: Hard cases in reported speech
intro: Read this before the difficult quiz. These traps hide in the situation, not in the tense table.

blocks.title: no backshift
items: **Reporting verb in the present or present perfect:** She **says** she is tired. He **has said** he is busy.
**General truths and facts that are still true:** The teacher said the earth **goes** round the sun.
**Past perfect stays:** 'I had met her.' → He said he **had met** her.
**Modals that already look back:** would, could, might, should, ought to do not change: 'You should rest.' → She said I **should** rest.

blocks.title: conditionals
items: **First conditional moves one step:** 'If I **see** her, I **will** tell her.' → He said that if he **saw** her, he **would** tell her.
**Second conditional stays:** 'If I **were** rich, I **would** travel.' → She said that if she **were** rich, she **would** travel.
**Third conditional stays:** 'If I **had known**, I **would have come**.' → He said that if he **had known**, he **would have come**.

blocks.title: two readings
items: **had + participle** in a report can come from **two** direct forms: 'I **saw** him.' and 'I **have seen** him.' both become He said he **had seen** him.
**must** as an obligation becomes **had to**, but **must** as a deduction stays: 'It **must** be true.' → She said it **must** be true.
**used to** does not change: 'I **used to** smoke.' → He said he **used to** smoke.

blocks.body: For a difficult report, work in four steps: (1) the reporting verb, (2) the verb tense, (3) pronouns, (4) time and place words.
